strengths: Identifies an important and previously unexplored vulnerability in concept erasure methods, addressing a critical gap in AI safety research
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across six erasure methods, three threat scenarios, and multiple metrics with thorough ablation studies
Novel application of backdoor techniques to circumvent concept erasure, introducing multiple EEB variants with different attack points and mechanisms
Well-motivated threat model with clear assumptions; solid technical soundness demonstrated through systematic results
Clear presentation with effective figures and well-structured exposition; promises code release for reproducibility with detailed supplementary material provided
Timely contribution that advances understanding of adversarial robustness in generative models and will likely motivate more robust defense development
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—primarily adapts existing backdoor and data poisoning techniques rather than introducing fundamentally new attack primitives
Threat model assumes white-box access and training data poisoning capability, which constrains practical threat realism and real-world applicability
Lacks concrete defense mechanisms or mitigation strategies; while identifying vulnerabilities is valuable, constructive solutions are minimal
Insufficient mechanistic analysis of why different erasure methods fail; missing analysis of failure mode commonalities or how combined erasure methods might improve robustness
No comprehensive evaluation of detection methods or defense strategies beyond brief mention of anomaly detection without empirical validation
Limited to text-to-image diffusion models and specific architectural versions; generalization to other generative models or domains not addressed
